messages:
incident-bot: Paging @maya (oncall) — high error rate detected for customer 'aurum' in dedicated-vpc pool 'eu-west-2-ded-3'. 5xxs + elevated latency across canary slice. auto-created incident #INC-35912 :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking alerts. @leo can you stand up?

leo (eng-runtime): here, looking at canary metrics now. I see token latency spikes and GPU util jumping to 98% on two hosts. traces show repeated OOM/retry loops for model-worker.

aleks (platform-eng): noticed infra autoscaler recently moved a few nodes off the pool for maintenance around 03:10 UTC — could be resource fragmentation. pulling node assignment.

nora (support): Tammy from Aurum is in the slack channel and says their frontend reports cascading failures for a subset of users. She wants ETA and mitigation plan.

tammy (customer-ops): Confirmed: about ~12% of their requests are 502s and the web team is seeing 5s+ response times. They're asking to reduce impact; they flagged the canary traffic slice.

maya (oncall): OK action plan: 1) cordon affected tenant + isolate from canary traffic; 2) unpin artifact and roll back canary to previous artifact; 3) if necessary, evacuate problematic hosts. I'll coordinate with you all.

leo (eng-runtime): Agreed. Running tenant cordon command now: 
```
redwood-admin isolate-tenant --tenant aurum --pool eu-west-2-ded-3 --reason "canary spike 35912"
```

deploy-bot: Command accepted. Queueing isolation workflow. Task ID: wf-aurum-35912-iso.

leo (eng-runtime): Isolation completed: tenant aurum moved to cordoned state, traffic removed from canary slice. Verifying routing table entries...

le o (eng-runtime): typo previous message, meant 'leo' — routing shows aurum now served from stable pool only. Canary slice traffic for aurum at 0%.

tammy (customer-ops): Confirmed from their side — errors dropped to ~6% but still seeing latency bumps. Thanks for the quick isolate.

aleks (platform-eng): Next step: check pinned artifact. aurum's canary was pinned to artifact v2.34.7 last deploy. Let's unpin and promote v2.33.1 as the canary fallback.

leo (eng-runtime): Running artifact unpin + staged rollback: 
```
redwood-deploy promote --tenant aurum --from v2.33.1 --to-canary --pool eu-west-2-ded-3 --staged 3m --weights 75,50,25
```

deploy-bot: Promotion workflow started. deployment-id: deploy-35912-aurum-promote. Rolling weights will be applied over 3m windows.

maya (oncall): While that runs, I'm watching GPU host states. If we see repeated OOMs, we'll cordon hosts and shift capacity. Also enabling additional KV cache for aurum to reduce model recompute.

leo (eng-runtime): Logs from canary controllers during rollout: 
```
[03:22:10] rollout-step: set weight 75% -> ok
[03:25:10] rollout-step: set weight 50% -> ok
[03:28:10] rollout-step: set weight 25% -> ok
[03:31:10] rollout-complete: canary now on v2.33.1 (rollback)
```

tammy (customer-ops): aurum reports error rates back to baseline ~0.5% and latency normalized. They want the canary kept at stable for now and will run their internal smoke tests for 30m.

nora (support): I'll schedule a follow-up call with Tammy + their SRE in 20 minutes to confirm. Sending preliminary incident summary to Aurora CSM.

aleks (platform-eng): Noted noisy hosts: host-324 and host-319 showed intermittent PCIe resets around 03:07-03:15. I've placed both hosts in quarantine and triggered a maintenance rebuild.

leo (eng-runtime): Added a bailout policy to prefer lower-latency kernels for aurum's typical prompt lengths; this should avoid expensive kernel paths that were thrashing memory.

maya (oncall): Paging @leo and @aleks for a quick postmortem draft after the smoke window: timeline, cause hypotheses (pinned artifact + low capacity due to node maintenance -> GPU hot spots), and next steps (improve canary throttles, add preflight checks for pinned artifacts under maintenance ops).

tammy (customer-ops): Aurum asks if we can temporarily increase their reserved burst capacity while they finish tests — they have a major batch job at 07:00 UTC. Could we grant one-off buff?

aleks (platform-eng): We can grant a temporary burst from spare capacity if SLA allows. I'll open a reserve action and set expiration at 08:30 UTC.

deploy-bot: Capacity grant enacted: grant-aurum-burst-35912 expires 172 minutes from now.

maya (oncall): Good. For the incident record: root cause provisional: pinned canary artifact v2.34.7 with a regression combined with reduced node availability -> concentrated GPU pressure -> model-worker retries and OOMs -> increased 5xx. Mitigation: isolate tenant from canary -> rollback canary to v2.33.1 -> quarantine noisy hosts -> temporary burst.

nora (support): Filing INC-35912 with the above mitigation steps and notifying account team. Tammy, I'll put the support-runbook notes in the ticket.

tammy (customer-ops): Thanks everyone. Aurum will monitor and will reach out if they see anything odd. Appreciate the fast turnaround. :heart:

maya (oncall): I'll keep the incident open for the smoke test window; if aurum confirms stable in 30m we'll close. Assigning follow-up to @leo and @aleks for the postmortem doc.

leo (eng-runtime): I'll start the postmortem draft and include telemetry charts, kernel traces, and the rollout logs.

aleks (platform-eng): I'll add the infra maintenance schedule overlap and propose an autoscaler tweak to avoid compaction of GPU capacity during rolling upgrades.

deploy-bot: Incident INC-35912 status: monitoring. will auto-close after 60m of stable metrics.

maya (oncall): closing note — we should consider adding an automated preflight that warns on pinned artifacts when pool capacity < X. adding to backlog.

nora (support): Closing loop with Aurum in the ticket once they confirm. Good job team. :clap:
